verdict.rationale: Mem0 documents a first-party `expiration_date` field on memories. Once that date passes, the memory stops surfacing in search without any cleanup job, and this works on both Platform and Open Source. That directly delivers the expiration-date route to keeping stale facts out of results. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of expiration behavior, and documented relative TTL or recency-weighted decay options.

support.subject: As a developer, I can make memories expire or decay — via TTL, expiration dates, or recency weighting — so stale facts stop surfacing

citations.quote: Set an expiration_date on a memory and Mem0 stops surfacing it once that date passes, so you don't need a cleanup job hunting for rows to delete.
Set an expiration date on a Mem0 memory and it stops surfacing in search once that date passes. Nothing is deleted. Works on Platform and Open Source.
